answer: Counterfactual Co-Signing Ledger. Each identity must co-sign a rotating public fable of its actions with a randomly assigned partner grove, where partners are drawn from separate coordination clusters. A cedar seal hash ties every signed claim to the pair, so a sybil must recruit independent partners per identity and cannot reuse one partner across many. Cost per identity: one unique co-signer and a live reciprocal signature, making N identities require N distinct counterparties.
